mainTopic: Advance payments, discounts and sharecropping: when a deal is fair business and when it looks like ריבית
overview: This amud deals with deals that can look like ריבית, meaning payment for waiting for money. It first finishes a ברייתא: a deal is allowed if the seller carries the risk, repaying produce in another town is allowed only if the borrower owns produce there, and donkey drivers may charge the cheaper town's price. רב פפא and רב אחא בריה דרב איקא give two business reasons for the drivers' leniency, and the reasons give different results for a new merchant. רב bought wheat this way but took less than the full amount, because an important person is stricter with himself. רבי יוחנן tells stories showing that such deals were not allowed with linen garments or metal scraps. רב and שמואל argue about buying an orchard's produce in advance at a discount, though רב agrees it is allowed with oxen, since their risk of loss is high. שמואל and רבא give practical advice on how to set up such deals so they are permitted. Finally, רבא defends his own deal with his sharecroppers against the charge that he takes ריבית.

steps.title: Who carries the risk decides the deal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its previous case. The deal is allowed if the seller carries the risk, and forbidden if the buyer carries it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is in the seller's responsibility, it is permitted. If it is in the buyer's responsibility, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the ברייתא in the middle. This line ends the case of a package being carried from place to place, and it gives the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller stays responsible for the goods until they arrive, this is a real sale, so it is not a loan. If the buyer takes on the risk right away, his money already 'belongs' in the deal. Any extra he gains then looks like payment for waiting, which is ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: in the possession of, meaning under someone's responsibility and risk

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'possession' does not mean who is holding the package. It means who loses out if something happens to it on the way.

phrases.english: In the seller's possession: permitted;
phrases.notes: 'Possession' here means the seller carries the risk if the goods get damaged or lost on the way.

phrases.english: in the buyer's possession: forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּרְשׁוּת מוֹכֵר – מוּתָּר, בִּרְשׁוּת לוֹקֵחַ – אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא's earlier package case, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A transfer deal is allowed only when the seller keeps the risk.

steps.title: Borrowing produce to repay it in another town
steps.stepSummary: Someone asks a traveler for his produce now and promises to repay him with produce in the town he is heading to. This is allowed only if the borrower really owns produce there.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person is carrying produce from one place to another. His friend meets him and says: 'Give them to me, and I will pay you back with produce I have in that place.' If he really has produce there, it is permitted. If not, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a new case. It is about lending produce now and being paid back in produce later, somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lending produce for produce is a problem because the price may go up, and then the lender gets back more value. If the borrower already owns that produce in the other town, it is as if he hands it over right now, so it is allowed. If he owns none, it is a risky produce loan, which is forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses the well-known rule of סאה בסאה. Lending produce for produce is allowed only when the borrower already has some of it.

phrases.english: One who transports produce from place to place,
his fellow found him and said to him:
Give them to me and I will repay you
with produce that I have in that place,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ פֵּירוֹת בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם – מוּתָּר,
phrases.english: if he has produce in that place, it is permitted;
and if not, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוֹלִיךְ פֵּירוֹת מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repaying produce in another town is allowed only if the borrower actually owns produce there.

steps.title: Donkey drivers may charge the cheaper town's price
steps.stepSummary: Donkey drivers may take money in an expensive town and set their price by the cheap town's rate. There is no worry of ריבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Donkey drivers may set prices in the expensive place the same as in the cheap place, and they do not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a surprising leniency for donkey drivers. This line sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The customer pays now and later gets goods worth more than the local price. That looks like a discount for paying early, which is normally a problem of ריבית. Even so, the ברייתא says this is allowed, without giving a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: donkey drivers who transport goods to sell

phrases.english: And donkey drivers set prices in the expensive place
phrases.notes: They take the customer's money now and deliver the goods later.

phrases.english: as in the cheap place, and they need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַחַמָּרִין מַעֲלִים בִּמְקוֹם הַיּוֹקֶר כְּבִמְקוֹם הַזּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last ruling of the ברייתא. It is a lenient case that the גמרא will now ask about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Donkey drivers may give the cheap town's price for money paid in the expensive town.

steps.title: Why are the donkey drivers allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the donkey drivers' leniency.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the donkey drivers' deal is allowed. This question sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying early to get a lower price normally looks like ריבית. So the גמרא needs a reason why the drivers' discount is not payment for the use of the money.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the drivers' discount is not considered ריבית.

steps.title: רב פפא: it opens the market for them
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the drivers are happy to sell cheaply because it gets them into the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is worth it to them, because this opens the gates of the market for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the first reason. The low price is a way to attract customers, not payment for waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drivers gain new customers and a foothold in a new market. Because of that, the discount is ordinary marketing, not a reward for the early money.

keyTerms.meaning: it is good for them, they are happy with it
gate, here meaning the entrance to a market

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is good for them, because the gates are opened for them.
phrases.notes: Opening the gates means getting into a new market and winning customers.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר נִיחָא לְהוּ דִּמְגַלּוּ לְהוּ תַּרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The discount brings the drivers new customers, so it is not ריבית.

steps.title: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא: they buy cheaply too
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא says the drivers are happy because the suppliers give them lower prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said: It is worth it to them, because prices are lowered for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different reason for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the drivers are not losing money. The suppliers give them a discount too, so selling cheaply is simply passing that on. Since they are not giving anything up, there is no hidden payment for the money.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Ika said:
It is good for them, because prices are lowered for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא אָמַר נִיחָא לְהוּ דְּמוֹזְלִי גַּבַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The drivers buy cheaply themselves, so their low price costs them nothing.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between רב פפא and רב אחא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks if the two reasons ever lead to different results. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reasons allow the normal case. The גמרא looks for a situation where one reason works and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is between them?
phrases.notes: Meaning: in what case would the two reasons give different answers?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares steps 5 and 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two reasons give different results.

steps.title: The difference: a new merchant
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a new merchant. רב פפא's reason fits him well, but רב אחא's reason does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a new merchant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two reasons differ in the case of a brand-new merchant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רב פפא, a new merchant needs to open the market most of all, so he may sell cheaply. Under רב אחא, suppliers would not yet give a newcomer a discount, so his low price would really be paid for by the early money. That makes it forbidden for him.

keyTerms.meaning: there is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: Donkey drivers may give the cheap price because it helps their business, not as payment for early money. רב פפא's reason (opening the market) allows a new merchant to do this, while רב אחא's reason (cheaper suppliers) does not.

phrases.english: The difference between them is a new merchant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ תַּגָּרָא חַדְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A new merchant is allowed according to רב פפא but not according to רב אחא.

steps.title: רב buys wheat through donkey drivers at a price between the two towns
steps.stepSummary: Wheat cost four סאה per סלע in סורא and six in כפרי. רב gave money to donkey drivers, took the road risk on himself, and accepted five סאה per סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: In סורא wheat sold at four סאה per סלע, and in כפרי at six. רב gave money to the donkey drivers, took on himself any accident on the road, and took five from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רב actually bought wheat from a cheaper town.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב took the risk of loss on the road onto himself. That means the wheat was already his once it was bought in כפרי, so this was a purchase and not a loan. Even so, he took only five סאה, not the full six of the כפרי price, and this sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Donkey drivers who carry goods between towns
An accident or loss on the road
Literally 'going'; here it means the market rate

phrases.english: In Sura they were going at four apiece,
phrases.notes: He means four סאה of wheat for one סלע.

phrases.english: in Kafri they were going at six apiece.
Rav gave money to the donkey drivers
and accepted upon himself any accident on the road,
phrases.notes: Some versions add the letter in square brackets; read it as part of the word.

phrases.english: and he took five from them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּסוּרָא אָזְלִי אַרְבָּעָה אַרְבְּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After discussing why donkey drivers agree to cheaper deals, the גמרא brings a case of what רב himself did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the buyer takes on the road risk, he may buy at the cheaper town's rate. רב still took only five סאה per סלע.

steps.title: Why didn't רב take six?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the deal was allowed, רב should have taken the full six סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him take six!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's behavior. If the deal was permitted, why did he take only five?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking on the road risk made the wheat רב's own purchase at the כפרי price. So there was nothing like ריבית here, and he should have been entitled to the full six.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him take (a challenge: 'he should have taken')

phrases.english: But let him take six!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִשְׁקוֹל שִׁיתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the five-סאה detail of the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's choice to take only five סאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If taking the risk makes the deal fully permitted, the full כפרי price of six should have been allowed.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: רב was stricter with himself because he was an important person.
steps.simpleTranslation: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב held himself to a higher standard because of who he was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Six would have been allowed by the strict law. But an important person must avoid even the look of ריבית, so רב stopped partway, at five.
steps.whatToRemember: The deal itself was permitted. רב's taking five was an extra stringency for an important person, not the basic law.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that taking six is forbidden. It is allowed; רב was simply being extra careful.

phrases.english: An important person is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם חָשׁוּב שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the deal was permitted, רב should have taken six.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six is permitted, but an important person stays further away from the appearance of ריבית.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks about metal scraps
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן whether this cheaper-rate arrangement also works for metal scraps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן: May one do this with metal scraps?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question: does the cheaper-rate deal that works for produce also work for scrap metal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the deals involved produce, like wheat, which has a known market price. רבי אסי wants to know whether scrap goods can be bought the same way.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yochanan:
What is the law about doing so with metal scraps?
phrases.notes: 'Doing so' means buying ahead of time at the cheaper rate, like the produce deals just discussed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the topic from produce to another kind of goods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the cheaper-rate purchase arrangement is allowed for metal scraps.

steps.title: רבי did not allow it with linen garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers with a story: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי wanted to do this with linen garments, and רבי stopped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי wanted to do so with linen garments, and רבי did not let him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by telling a story, which suggests the answer is no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving a rule, רבי יוחנן tells of a similar case in which רבי forbade the deal for linen garments. The implication is that metal scraps, like linen garments, would also not be allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּיקֵּשׁ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei wanted
to do so with linen garments,
and Rebbi did not allow him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בִּיקֵּשׁ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אסי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. A similar deal with linen garments was forbidden by רבי.

steps.title: Another version: רבי wanted to do it with scraps
steps.stepSummary: Some say the roles were reversed: רבי wanted to do this with metal scraps, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי did not let him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבי wanted to do so with metal scraps, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי did not let him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same story, with the people switched and scraps instead of linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the details change: who wanted to do it, who stopped him, and which goods were involved. In both versions the deal was not allowed, so the answer to רבי אסי stays the same.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rebbi wanted to do so with metal scraps,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הִנִּיחוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei did not allow him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the story in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deal was not allowed. In this version the case was about scraps, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי was the one who objected.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree on the result: this deal was not allowed for these goods.

steps.title: Buying an orchard's produce ahead of time: רב forbids, שמואל permits
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue about paying in advance, at a cheaper price, for the future produce of an orchard.
steps.simpleTranslation: An orchard: רב forbids and שמואל permits.
steps.whatsHappening: A new case: may one pay now, at a lower price, for an orchard's future produce? רב says no, and שמואל says yes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side's reason is not given yet. The next step will explain why each one holds the way he does.

phrases.english: An orchard:
phrases.notes: He means buying the orchard's produce ahead of time for a cheaper price.

phrases.english: Rav forbids and Shmuel permits.

steps.triggerLanguage: פַּרְדֵּיסָא, רַב אָסַר וּשְׁמוּאֵל שָׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case of buying in advance at a discount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רב forbids buying an orchard's produce in advance at a discount, and שמואל permits it.

steps.title: The reasons of רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב: the produce will be worth more later, so the discount looks like payment for waiting. שמואל: the produce might spoil, so it does not look like payment for waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב forbids: since later it will be worth more, it looks like he is paying him for waiting. שמואל permits: since it may spoil, it does not look like payment for waiting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying someone for waiting for his money is the heart of ריבית. רב sees that the produce will likely be worth more by harvest, so the discount looks like a reward for waiting. שמואל points out that the buyer takes a real risk of spoilage, so this is a genuine gamble and not a reward for waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: Payment for waiting (the core idea of ריבית)

phrases.english: Rav forbids,
since later on it is worth more,
it looks like payment to him for waiting.
And Shmuel permits,
since there can be spoilage in it,

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִיחֲזֵי כִּי אֲגַר נְטַר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: it does not look like payment to him for waiting.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָסַר, כֵּיוָן דִּלְקַמֵּיהּ שָׁוְיָא טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the argument in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether the deal looks like payment for waiting depends on how much real risk of loss the buyer takes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that real risk is what separates an honest deal from something that looks like ריבית.

steps.title: רב agrees about young oxen
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא says that רב agrees the deal is permitted with oxen, because losses with them are common.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: רב agrees about oxen, whose losses are great.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא limits רב's ban: when buying oxen ahead of time, even רב would allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oxen often die or get hurt, so the buyer's risk is large and obvious. With that much risk, the discount clearly does not look like payment for waiting, so רב agrees to שמואל's reasoning here.
steps.whatToRemember: רב forbids buying an orchard's produce ahead of time at a discount, but agrees it is permitted with oxen, because the buyer's risk of loss is large.

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Chiya said:
And Rav agrees regarding oxen, since their losses are great.
phrases.notes: He means buying young oxen now to receive them later; raising them often brings losses, since some may die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא: וּמוֹדֵי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב's ban from step 15, using the risk reasoning of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רב permits buying oxen in advance at a discount, because the risk of loss is high.

steps.title: שמואל's advice to buyers of vine branches
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells people who pay in advance for vine branches to do some work on the land, so they become partners and the deal is not treated like a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to those who buy vine branches: Turn over the soil yourselves, so that you acquire a share in the land itself. If you don't, it is like a loan to you, and it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives practical advice to people who pay ahead of time, at a discount, for vine branches that will be cut later. He tells them to work the land a little so the deal becomes a partnership.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer just hands over money now and collects later at a lower price, it looks like a loan paid back with extra, which is רבית. By working the soil, the buyer becomes a partner in the land itself. A partner who shares in the field is not a lender, so the discount is no longer payment for waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: those who buy vine branches (shoots of grapevines)
turn over the soil, meaning do some farm work

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key principle: being a partner who shares in the field is different from being a lender, so a deal that would be רבית can become permitted.

phrases.english: Shmuel said to them,
to those who buy vine branches:
phrases.notes: These buyers pay now for branches that will be cut from the vines later.

phrases.english: Turn over the soil,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דִּקְנֵי לְכוּ גּוּפָא דְאַרְעָא,
phrases.english: so that you acquire a share in the land itself,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – הָוְיָא לְכוּ כְּהַלְוָאָה וְאָסוּר.
phrases.english: and if not, it is like a loan for you, and it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְהָנְהוּ דְּשָׁבְשִׁי שִׁבְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of paying in advance at a discount (steps 15-17) with a practical case and a way to make it permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer who pays ahead for vine branches must do some work on the land to become a partner; otherwise the deal counts as a loan and is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא's advice to field guards
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells field guards to help at the threshing floor, so their wages only come due at the end, when the discount they get is not payment for waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to those who guard fields: Go out and turn over the grain at the threshing floor, so that your wages are not due until that time. Wages are only due at the end of the job, and at that time the owners are simply giving you a discount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the guards a practical tip: keep working until the threshing is done. That way their job is not over yet when they get paid at a lower price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guards get paid in grain at a discount. If their job had ended earlier, their wages would already be owed, and the discount would look like payment for waiting for the money. By working until the threshing floor, their wage only becomes due then, so the discount at that moment is just a cheaper sale, not רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: is only due at the end of the job
giving a discount, lowering the price

steps.confusionAlert: The discount itself does not change. What changes is when the wage becomes owed. A discount on money already owed looks like payment for waiting; a discount at the moment the wage first comes due does not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רָבָא לְהָנְהוּ דִּמְנַטְּרִי בָּאגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel piece of practical advice: like שמואל, רבא shows how to arrange a deal so the discount is not payment for waiting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Guards who keep working until the threshing is done have wages that only become due at the end. A discount given at that moment is not payment for waiting, so it is permitted.

steps.title: The רבנן accuse רבא of taking interest
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רבא: other landowners take four and remove the sharecropper in ניסן, but רבא waits until אייר and takes six, which looks like payment for waiting.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: The Master is eating רבית! Everyone else takes four and removes the sharecropper in ניסן, but the Master waits for them until אייר and takes six!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבא's own behavior with his sharecroppers. They say the extra two he takes looks like payment for letting them stay an extra month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the owner takes four and sends the sharecropper away in ניסן. רבא lets them stay until אייר and collects six. The רבנן argue the extra two is a fee for waiting, which is exactly the kind of payment that counts as רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: the Master, a respectful way to address a rabbi
a sharecropper who works the field for a share of the crop

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
The Master is eating interest!
For everyone takes four
phrases.notes: Four measures of grain as the owner's payment.

phrases.english: and removes the sharecropper in Nisan,
but the Master waits for them until Iyar
and takes six!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: קָא אָכֵיל מָר רִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבא's advice to others to a challenge against רבא's own practice, using the same idea of payment for waiting.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's practice of letting his sharecroppers stay until אייר and collecting six instead of four.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra two measures seem to be a fee for giving the sharecropper an extra month, which is payment for waiting and therefore רבית.

steps.title: רבא defends his practice
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the land is bound to the sharecropper until he finishes; others hurt their sharecroppers by removing them in ניסן, while he lets them profit by staying until אייר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to them: You are the ones acting improperly. The land is bound to the sharecropper. If you remove them in ניסן, you cause them a big loss. I wait for them until אייר, and I let them earn a lot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by turning it around. He says the others are wrong to remove sharecroppers early, and his longer arrangement is the fair one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא explains that the sharecropper has a right to the land until he finishes his work. Removing him in ניסן cuts him off before he can gain fully, so it is a loss to him. Staying until אייר is the proper length of the deal, so the six is a fair price for a full season, not an extra fee for waiting.

keyTerms.meaning: not according to the law, improperly
is bound, has a lien on it

steps.whatToRemember: A higher payment is not רבית when it matches a longer, fair use of the field. רבא's six measures pay for the full season the sharecropper is entitled to, while the others shortchange their sharecroppers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that we must look at what the payment is really for. If it pays for real extra use, it is a fair price, not a fee for waiting.

phrases.english: He said to them: You are the ones acting improperly,
the land is bound to the sharecropper.
If you remove them in Nisan,
you cause them a big loss.
I wait for them until Iyar,
and I let them profit a great deal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַתּוּן קָא עָבְדִיתוּן שֶׁלֹּא כַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the רבנן's charge that רבא takes רבית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the facts: the extra time is the sharecropper's right, so the higher payment matches a longer, fair deal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן thought the extra two measures paid רבא for waiting an extra month before taking back his field.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the land is bound to the sharecropper until he finishes, staying until אייר is the proper deal. The six measures are a fair price for that, and removing sharecroppers in ניסן is what is actually wrong.
